title: ¿Y es casado usted?
desc: In four minutes they know your age, your work and whether you are married
setting: You sat down on the patio to wait for Roberto and three women have arrived instead.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¿Y usted vive solo en ese cuarto?
steps.en: And do you live alone in that room?

options.es: Solo, doña. Con mi maleta y nada más.
options.en: On my own, doña. With my suitcase and nothing else.
options.feedback: Answer and give her one detail more than she asked for. That is what turns a question into a conversation here.
Fine. In a patio full of people a second word keeps it friendly.

options.en: Why do you want to know?
options.feedback: Nothing is being asked of you. Where you live, your work and your family are the first three questions anyone gets.
One word and no explanation. You will be asked this by everybody you meet for the next year.
True. Soltero is the word she was waiting for and it costs you nothing.

options.en: That is none of your business.
options.feedback: Refusing the question is far stranger here than the question. She asked because she likes you.

steps.speaker: Vecina
steps.es: ¡Ay, soltero! ¿Y no quiere una mujer nica?
steps.en: Oh, single! And you do not want a Nicaraguan wife?

options.en: Ideay, doña, what do you say?
options.feedback: She is teasing you and you played. Being teased is being included, and answering in kind ends it well.
A calm answer to a joke. Nothing goes wrong and nothing happens either.
You answered a joke as if it were an offer. The patio will go quiet for a second.

options.es: Trabajo en mi casa, doña. Casi todo el día.
options.en: I work at home, doña. Most of the day.
options.feedback: Plain and concrete. Working from the house needs saying, or the whole street will wonder why you are always in.
Enough. Where you work matters as much as what you do, on a street where everyone sees everyone.

options.en: I do not know how to explain it to you.
options.feedback: That answer travels. By tonight nobody on the block will be sure what you do for money.
